heading: Where to Eat in West Kelowna
title: Where to Eat in West Kelowna | Okanagan Roam
description: Where to eat in West Kelowna: diner breakfasts, bakeries, taco stands, winery dining rooms, lake-view patios, BBQ and beer, and vegan-friendly kitchens.
intro: West Kelowna sits across the bridge from Kelowna, and it eats better than its size suggests. There are old-school breakfast diners on the Westside, family-run kitchens in Westbank, and winery dining rooms up on the slopes above the lake. This guide picks a few of each, from cheap and quick to a long dinner with a view.

Many patios and winery kitchens cut back their hours from November to April, so check each listing's hours before you head out. For the full list, see all {page:/west-kelowna/restaurants|West Kelowna restaurants}.

sections.heading: Breakfast & brunch
sections.lead: West Kelowna does the classic breakfast well. Come hungry.

items.name: Cherry Pit Restaurant
items.text: a no-frills greasy spoon that regulars call the best breakfast stop in the Okanagan. Order the classic breakfast and expect a generous plate.

items.name: Pepper Pot Grill
items.text: a cozy diner serving comfort food. The gravy is a standout and the bacon comes from Bonanza Meats. The lot is small, so expect a short wait.

items.name: Cozy Nook Cafe & Bar
items.text: a bright all-day breakfast and lunch spot on Main St with fast, friendly service. Try the avocado toast or the coffee glory pancakes.

items.name: Smitty's
items.text: a family restaurant with a Ukrainian menu next to the diner classics. Regulars recommend the borscht, and there's a play area for kids.

items.name: Cafe Bella Bean
items.text: the owner remembers your order, and board games are out for anyone who wants to stay a while.

items.name: The Ryse Breadworks & Coffeehouse
items.text: a quiet bakery-cafe with a wind-screened patio. Dogs are welcome, and a water dish is already out for them.

items.name: Two Donkeys Bakery (West Kelowna)
items.text: known for its pesto breakfast wraps. Add a flaky chocolate croissant.

items.name: A Touch of Austria
items.text: a musical garden café at the home of a pastry chef and performer. Expect Viennese coffee, Austrian chocolates and Sachertorte, often with live piano. It runs Friday to Sunday afternoons and you must reserve at least 48 hours ahead. Outdoor seating runs April through October.

items.name: Kekuli Cafe - West Kelowna
items.text: an Indigenous-owned café with a welcoming feel. The bannock tacos are the dish to order.

items.name: Smoke Shack Deli
items.text: a smokehouse deli that makes everything in-house. The meat is smoked on site for 20 hours.

items.name: MEX-KELOWNA TACOS
items.text: a taco stand that many reviewers call the best Mexican food in the Okanagan. The owner walks each guest through the menu, so let them guide you.

items.name: Gians Tandoori Corner
items.text: a down-to-earth Punjabi restaurant where the owner helps first-timers choose. Try the Amritsari kulcha and the gulab jamun.

sections.heading: Dinner worth booking
sections.lead: The winery dining rooms are the big draw here. For more across the valley, see our {page:/guides/okanagan-winery-restaurants|winery restaurants guide}.

items.name: Old Vines Restaurant
items.text: the fine-dining room at Quails' Gate Winery, with lake and mountain views. Order the haskap-cured salmon or the 63 Acres beef tenderloin. Staff are patient with young families.

items.name: Tula Restaurant @ Little Straw Vineyards
items.text: Indian-fusion cooking at a winery, with patio seats looking out over the working vineyard. Vegan diners can order with confidence.

items.name: The Modest Butcher Kitchen + Market
items.text: a steakhouse at Mt. Boucherie Estate Winery. The signature cut is the Tomahawk steak, and staff are patient with toddlers.

items.name: 31 Charkay
items.text: a modern, warm restaurant attached to Grizzli Winery. Steaks come cooked right, the arancini are crispy, and there are gluten-free options. Ask for the patio.

items.name: Two Brothers Mexican Restaurant
items.text: a small, cozy spot that regulars love for consistent, authentic cooking. The pozole keeps them coming back.

items.name: 19 Okanagan Grill + Bar
items.text: above the golf course, with a view over the fairways and Okanagan Lake. Twinkle lights come on across the patio at sunset.

items.name: Annie's Beach Cafe & Lounge
items.text: heated dining domes keep the beach view going when it cools off. There's room for kids to play nearby.

items.name: The Landing Kitchen + Bar
items.text: a resort restaurant known for its Saturday prime rib special. Tell staff how you want it cooked.

items.name: Shannon Lake Restaurant
items.text: a golf-course restaurant overlooking the lake. Regulars come for Wednesday wing night and prime rib Sunday.

items.name: Lakesider Brewing
items.text: right on the lake, with a dog-friendly patio, wood-fired pizza and a strong beer list.

items.name: The Hatching Post Brewery & Smokery
items.text: a lively BBQ smokehouse with live western music. Order the brisket with something from the big craft beer list. Happy hour runs weekdays.

items.name: Truck 59 Ciderhouse
items.text: crisp cider, open lawns and lakeside lounging. The Truck Yard also pours Hatching Post beer, cocktails and JPC wine.

items.name: Whiski-Jacks Pub
items.text: a longstanding pub near the Smith Creek mountain biking trails, so it suits a post-ride stop. There's a patio, free pool and a happy hour.

items.name: Pandanus Thai Restaurant
items.text: authentic Thai, all made to order, so changes are easy. The kitchen has removed egg to make a dish fully vegan. Ask freely.

items.name: Everest Indian Restaurant
items.text: an Indian-Nepalese kitchen that has veganized a coconut curry on request. Ask about changes without worry.

items.name: Bamboo Chopsticks Vietnamese Restaurant
items.text: a grandpa-run kitchen cooking comfort food. The curry tofu is the order, and it wins over every age group.
